old_wording: The client’s cloud bill was not high because the business had outgrown its infrastructure. It was high because years of unmanaged cloud usage had created silent waste. Servers were overprovisioned, storage was not lifecycle-managed, deployments were difficult to maintain, and the infrastructure had no clear cost-control process. KP Infotech reviewed the complete setup, identified unnecessary spend, migrated workloads into a leaner environment, introduced Docker-based deployment management with Coolify, and optimized AWS S3 storage using lifecycle policies and intelligent tiering. The result was a major reduction in recurring cloud cost, better infrastructure control, easier deployments, and a setup the client could maintain and scale with more confidence.

old_wording: The remote work revolution created demand for collaboration tools beyond Slack and Zoom. Existing solutions fragmented workflows across chat, video calls, doc editing, and project management. Teams wasted hours context-switching between 5-8 tools daily. The founders envisioned an all-in-one workspace combining real-time messaging, video, collaborative docs, task management, and knowledge base—with seamless integration eliminating app fatigue.

The platform needed enterprise-grade security (SSO, audit logs, data residency) while remaining simple enough for small teams.

old_wording: We interviewed 120 remote teams to map collaboration workflows. Findings: 67% switched apps 20+ times daily, 54% missed important updates buried in channels, and 72% wanted AI to surface relevant information proactively. We designed a unified interface with three core surfaces: messaging streams, collaborative documents, and video rooms—all accessible within one window, eliminating constant app switching.

old_wording: The platform used a microservices architecture: Next.js frontend, Elixir for real-time messaging (leveraging Phoenix Channels), Yjs CRDT for collaborative editing, WebRTC mesh architecture for peer-to-peer video (fallback to SFU for large calls), PostgreSQL for persistent data, and Elasticsearch for search. The real-time sync layer achieved sub-100ms message delivery and conflict-free document editing even with 30+ simultaneous collaborators.

old_wording: Community Trust Credit Union served 75,000 members with assets of $850M but was losing ground to digital-first competitors. Their existing online banking system was built on a 15-year-old platform with poor mobile experience, limited functionality, and frequent outages. Member surveys revealed that 58% were considering switching to competitors due to digital banking frustration, and the credit union was losing 3-5% of accounts annually to millennial and Gen-Z demographics.

old_wording: We led a comprehensive 8-week discovery and design sprint, conducting 85 member interviews, analyzing 2 years of support tickets, and benchmarking 12 best-in-class digital banking experiences. Our research identified key pain points: complex navigation (avg 5.2 clicks for basic transfers), unclear error messages, lack of spending insights, and slow load times (avg 7.3s for account summary). We created persona-driven user journeys for 5 key member segments and validated designs through 4 rounds of usability testing.

The visual design used calming blues and greens to build trust while maintaining the credit union's brand identity.

Savings Goals: Visual progress tracking with automatic round-up transfers to goals. Card Controls: Real-time ability to freeze/unfreeze cards, set spending limits, and block specific merchant categories.

CloudFront CDN distributed assets globally for optimal performance.

Batch processes reconciled data nightly, with automated alerting for any discrepancies.
